name: Deployment: pipelines, Git, PBIP, TMDL, XMLA, Tabular Editor

why.matters: Without source control and promotion between environments, every change is made live in production and nobody can say what changed or roll it back.
why.failure: Two developers overwrite each other's published model; a measure silently changes and the board pack is wrong for a week.
why.use: PBIP + Git for every shared model; deployment pipelines or Fabric Git integration to move Dev → Test → Prod.
why.avoid: Editing the production model directly through XMLA as a habit; it bypasses review and breaks .pbix download.

verified.context: PBIP overview and PBIR report format (Microsoft Learn, 2026-09-23); deployment pipelines docs

steps: Save your report as a Power BI Project: File → Save as → .pbip. Current Desktop builds save the model as TMDL and the report in PBIR, the enhanced report format that is now the default. Older builds needed preview switches for both.
Initialise a Git repo, commit. Open the folder: .SemanticModel/definition/*.tmdl and .Report/definition.
Change a measure in Desktop, save, git diff. Then change the same measure directly in the .tmdl file while the project is open: Desktop detects the external change and offers to apply it.
Connect the workspace to a Git branch (Fabric Git integration). Commit from Desktop, sync in the Service.
asg.exp: A readable diff showing exactly one measure expression change.

steps: Create a deployment pipeline with the three workspaces. Assign Dev.
Deploy to Test. Add a deployment rule that changes the Environment parameter (from the Intermediate parameter assignment) to "Test".
Compare Test vs Dev after changing a measure in Dev: the pipeline shows "Different". Deploy again.
Deploy only the semantic model, not the report, using selective deployment.
asg.exp: Prod points at the Prod source without anyone editing the PBIX.

steps: Open the model in Tabular Editor 2. Write a C# script that creates, for every measure ending in "Sales", a sibling measure "{name} PY" using SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR.
Run Best Practice Analyzer with the standard rules. Fix every violation, or document why not.
Use the XMLA endpoint (needs PPU/capacity) to open the published model, rename a measure, save. Note that the model can no longer be downloaded as PBIX.
Format all DAX with the built-in formatter.
asg.exp: BPA shows 0 errors. You can list three BPA rules you disagree with and why.

steps: Tag a Git commit as v1.0. Deploy. Make a breaking change (rename a column a report uses). Deploy.
Roll back by checking out the tag and syncing to the workspace.
Write a one-paragraph release note template you would send to report authors.
asg.exp: The broken visual is fixed after the rollback without touching the report.

int.q: PBIX vs PBIP: why does it matter for a team?
int.a: PBIX is a binary blob: no diffs, no merges, one person at a time. PBIP splits model (TMDL) and report (JSON) into text files that Git can diff and merge, and enables CI/CD and code review.

int.q: What does a deployment rule change and what can it not change?
int.a: Data source connections and parameter values per stage. It cannot change measures, RLS role membership or report content; those come from the deployed item.

int.q: After editing a model via XMLA, why can't you download the PBIX anymore?
int.a: The Service model has diverged from any PBIX; Desktop cannot round-trip arbitrary TOM changes. Your source of truth becomes the TMDL in Git.

int.q: How do you deploy a model without triggering a full refresh?
int.a: Deploy metadata only; the pipeline preserves data if the model structure allows. For incremental-refresh models, apply the refresh policy without data and refresh partitions in batches.

int.q: What is the difference between Fabric Git integration and deployment pipelines, and do you use both?
int.a: Git integration = source control and collaboration (branches, PRs). Pipelines = promotion between environments with rules. Typically Git for Dev, pipelines from Dev → Test → Prod, or Git-based deployment via API for full CI/CD.

o: A text serialisation of the tabular model definition
ass.why: Tabular Model Definition Language: one file per table with measures, columns, relationships in plain text.
Rules rewrite connection and parameter values on data items.

ass.q: Save your model as PBIP, write a Tabular Editor script that adds a description to every measure lacking one, commit, and show the git diff line count.
ass.hint: foreach(var m in Model.AllMeasures) if(string.IsNullOrEmpty(m.Description)) m.Description = "TODO";

ass.q: Best Practice Analyzer rule "Avoid bi-directional relationships" fires. Best response:
o: Justify or remove each; bridge-table security filters are a valid exception
ass.why: Rules are guidance; document justified exceptions.
